title: Data & Publications
before:
Data

  • Annual Report for School Transportation Safety, Training, and Personnel (ED545) are posted on the NEO Data System Dashboard.
  • Annual Report for School Transportation Expenditures and School Bus Inventory (ED 546) are posted on the NEO Data System Dashboard

Maine School Bus Purchase Program

The purpose of the Maine School Bus Purchase Program is to achieve the most equitable distribution of limited dollars to maintain a modern safe fleet of school buses and respond to emergency special bus needs.  An overview of the School Bus Purchase Program includes the following charts:

  • History of district applications and state approvals
  • History of dollars available vs requested
  • History of age range of approved school buses
  • History of average miles when a school bus is retired
  • History of program budget

Publications

  • American Society of Civil Engineers Report Card with America’s infrastructure scores and State infrastructure facts.  These national and state reports include transportation information. 
  • Maine Commercial Driver License Manual. Includes school bus driver’s section.
  • Maine Motor Vehicle Inspection Manual. Includes school bus section.
  • National School Transportation Specifications & Procedures adopted by the 17th National Congress on School Transportation. This national standard is the best practice for areas not addressed by law or rule. The 2015 copy is current. The next National Congress on School Transportation will be in May of 2025.  The 2020 National Congress on School Transportation was cancelled due to Covid.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 2 links on this page open a file — 2 PDF — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Jumbotron callouts become notes
decisions.why: 2 callouts are built as a Bootstrap jumbotron, which the component list replaced with dc-note and which Bootstrap itself removed in version 5. Same content, the site's own callout.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 5 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Run a label into the line it labels
decisions.why: 1 label sits alone in a paragraph with the sentence it labels in the next one — two blocks, two margins and a line break to say one thing. Down a list of exclusions that reads as a column of orphaned labels. Run in with a colon, which is how a term and its definition are set. The only character added is the colon.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 4 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
